paper_title: Discovering QCD-Coupled Axion Dark Matter with Polarization Haloscopes
notes: Projection (SNR>=2) for a proposed 'polarization haloscope' targeting the QCD axion-gluon coupling. The exclusion plot (Fig. 2) is on the 1/fa (GeV^-1) vs ma (eV) plane, spanning roughly ma ~ 1e-7 to 1e-4 eV and 1/fa ~ 1e-14 to 1e-5 GeV^-1. This is essentially a bound on the axion decay constant fa, hence AxionMass coupling type is most appropriate (the physical observable is the oscillating EDM dn ~ theta_a, related to gluon coupling and fa). No numerical table of the projected sensitivity curves is provided; only a figure exists, so no reliable data points could be extracted. Pre-analysis hint suggested AxionEDM, but the main exclusion plot y-axis is 1/fa not d_n, so AxionMass was chosen. Three benchmarks: 100L prototype (thermal), hyperpolarized cubic meter, post-discovery upgrade (tint=1yr). | Vision: This is a projected sensitivity plot with y-axis 1/f_a (GeV^-1) vs m_a (eV), NOT a standard exclusion limit. The y-axis is the inverse decay constant 1/f_a, not f_a or m_a as the AxionMass type expects. The traced 'lower boundary' here is the green QCD Axion theory line (canonical m_a-f_a relation from Eq. 2: m_a=5.7 ueV x 10^12 GeV/f_a). The shaded regions (blue scanning setups, CASPEr, storage ring) are projections, and SN1987A/Sun (gray) are upper-region constraints. Coupling type mapping to AxionMass is approximate since y-axis is 1/f_a, not f_a in GeV.
